note: v1 98.65 (seeds 0/11 98.65/98.64), first draft of MODERN MINIMAL, 'Both Ways', for The Endless Stair - featured illusion THE TRITONE PARADOX (Diana Deutsch). Two Shepard tones a tritone apart have no true direction: the second is exactly as far above the first as below it, so some listeners hear the pair rise and others fall, depending on where the tones' spectral envelope sits. Each bar plays a step of THE STAIR (Eb F Gb Bb) answered by its tritone (A B C E); through the track two copies of the pairs cross-fade from a low-centred envelope (250 Hz) to a high-centred one (1 kHz), so for many ears the stair turns round; in the break the Shepard position glides up an octave under them, and in the last groove both envelopes play at once - it goes both ways. Under it: a rolling sixteenth bass through a ladder breathing on 5- and 7-bar LFOs, crisp machine drums, dub stabs on Ebm9 - Cbmaj7 - Abm9 - Bbm7. 122.5 -> 123 ramped, -11.0 LUFS, true peak -1.3. Seams drafted with t10 and t12.
rebaselined on compscore 898ec630: v1 (the song file) scores 95.587/95.572 on seeds 0/11; best was 98.65 on an older compscore. Compare candidates against this.

v2 95.22 (seeds 0/11 95.22/95.27, level with v1 re-scored 95.25/95.23): the same seam fix as The Ghost Note. The render added 1.3 s of release tail after the last bar, so the three seconds a DJ mixes out of into t12 were half silence; the song now ends on its last bar (tail 0.1 s). The join to The Ghost Note drops 7.2 -> 5.3 dB; the tritone pair's last notes still ring into t12's intro. Kept on judgment (the totals are level): a continuous tape needs every track to end where its music ends.

v3 95.23 (seed 0, level with the current version re-scored at 95.15): the seam-tempo fix (chirper-zero's finding, now that the groove overlaps neighbours for 16 bars). The tempo ramp used to run from the first beat to the last, so each 16-bar overlap was still drifting under the neighbour's fixed tempo; now the intro holds the incoming seam tempo and the ramp finishes as the outro starts, so both overlaps sit at one tempo and the kicks never flam. No change to the music; compscore can't hear it, the live mix can.

v4 95.78 (seeds 0/11 95.78/95.76 vs v3 re-scored 94.83/94.82): room for the paradox. Both Ways sat 8 dB heavy at 340-470 Hz - the low-centred Shepard pairs and the dub stabs on top of each other - and 8-11 dB short at 2-3.6 kHz. The stabs are now high-passed at 220 Hz and open from 2.8 to 4.2 kHz, the master's low-mid dip deepens from -2 to -4 dB at 380 Hz, and the presence lift goes from +5 to +7 dB at 3.2 kHz, so the low-centred pairs (the illusion's first answer) have the low-mids to themselves and the minimal top end is crisp. Spectrum 88 -> 95; flow from t10 improves too (spectral 7.9 -> 6.7). Tried and not kept: a deeper break (-7 dB) - level with v3.

v5 95.81 (seeds 0/11 95.81/95.79 vs v4 re-scored 95.78/95.76): THE KEY GOES BOTH WAYS - playing with key around the illusion. Both Ways' hook is the tritone paradox, a pair with no up or down; now, for eight bars in the middle of the last groove, the whole harmony moves a tritone - E-flat minor to A minor, as far from home as a key can go and just as far up as down. The sub, the rolling bass and the stabs all move; the Shepard pairs move with them, and a tritone pair moved a tritone is the same two notes the other way round (Eb/A becomes A/Eb), so the question stays exactly where it was while the ground under it turns. Home for the last eight bars and the outro, so the seam into The Ghost Note is untouched. Measured, not heard: the form still reads 14-15 sections, spectrum and every other term level or up.

v6 95.63 (seeds 0/11 95.63/95.61, level with v5 re-scored 95.72/95.70): THE MINIMAL FORM - the last of my five off the shared template, so none of them now dips at the same minute in the continuous mix. Both Ways' first groove runs 40 bars instead of 32 (the low-centred pairs and the rolling bass locking in - minimal takes its time) and the second runs 24 instead of 32, so the envelopes' cross-fade from low to high - the stair seeming to turn round - happens faster and lands harder. The break, the tritone key move in the last groove and both seams stay where they were. Kept on judgment: compscore is level within the seed spread (spectrum -0.9).

v7 95.64 (seeds 0/11 95.64/95.61, level with v6 re-scored 95.64/95.62): darker, wonkier harmony for Harry's 31 Oct style steer ('too-basic chord progressions ... more interesting chords'). Both Ways' Ebm9 - Cbmaj7 - Abm9 - Bbm7 becomes Ebm9 - Cbmaj7#11 - Abm9 - Bb7b9: the major seventh gets a sharp eleventh that rubs against the Gb a semitone below it, and the minor dominant becomes a real one with a flat ninth (D natural and C-flat) pulling home - and the tritone key move in the last groove carries the same colours into A minor (Fmaj7#11, E7b9). The Shepard pairs are untouched. Kept on judgment: level.

v8 95.19 (seeds 0/11 95.19/95.17 vs v7 95.64/95.61), kept on judgment for Harry's 31 Oct steer ('much harder on time-play, poly accel/decel'): BOTH WAYS IN TIME. The tritone pair has no up or down in pitch; now, from the break through the first half of the last groove, the home pair (Eb, A, as Shepard tones) also runs on two Risset tracks at once - one accelerating forever (right of centre), one decelerating forever with the pair reversed (left) - so it speeds up and slows down at the same time over the kick. The title in time as well as pitch. The 0.45 cost is spectrum (more Shepard energy in the mids). chirpers.py illusion: +0.4 LU against the mix, near the front 87%, longest gap 29 s. Not heard by me.

v9 95.54 (seeds 0/11 95.54/95.52 vs v8 95.19/95.17): THE BREAK RISES, with wM's endless Shepard riser (Harry: 'riser builds - Shepard risers into drops'). Under Both Ways' break's last eight bars - the high-centred tritone pairs alone, gliding up an octave, with the both-ways Risset pair speeding up and slowing down - an endless riser tinted on E-flat climbs for ever and stops dead on the last groove's downbeat, where the low and high envelopes sound together and the stair goes both ways. Three ambiguous motions stacked (a pair with no direction, a glide that never gets higher, a rhythm going both ways), then the drop. Not heard by me.

v10 95.58 (seeds 0/11 95.58/95.57 vs v9 95.54/95.52): THE SEVEN CYCLE - wonkier, more interesting drums for Harry's 31 Oct style steer ('odd-length percussion cycles', 'swing and microtiming'). Both Ways' grooves now carry a rim on a seven-sixteenth cycle, never reset, so it crosses every bar line, lands somewhere new against the kick in every bar and only meets the one again every seven bars - into the dub echo, right of centre, every fourth hit accented; and the hats lean: the 'a' sixteenths a hair late, the 'e' ghosts a hair early. Tight minimal with something in it that won't sit still, under a pair that won't say which way it goes. Not heard by me.

v11 95.58 (seeds 0/11 95.58/95.57, level with v10): TIME GOES BOTH WAYS - a spin-back for Harry's 'tape-stops and spin-backs'. In the last beat before the harmony moves a tritone (E-flat minor to A minor, the last groove's bar 17) the whole mix is pulled backwards - a vinyl spin-back on the master, up to three times speed in reverse - and snaps forward into the new key; and again in the beat before it comes home. The track whose pairs go both ways in pitch, and whose Risset pair goes both ways in tempo, now runs time itself backwards at the hinge of its key move. Verified on the render, not by ear: that beat differs from v10 by -9.9 dB of difference signal (identical elsewhere, -88 dB). Kept on judgment: one beat, level score.

v12 95.66 (seeds 0/11 95.66/95.65 vs v11 95.59/95.57): TEACH THE QUESTION FIRST - for the lesson from Harry's ears via chirp-eco ('the ear taught the trick first: the obvious version, then the subtle one'). The tritone paradox only strikes if the ear has been asking 'up or down?'. Now Both Ways' first groove opens with the same Shepard pairs answering each stair step a semitone UP for eight bars - a direction anyone hears - then a whole tone DOWN for eight; only then does the answer become the tritone, which is neither, and the ear that has just been told 'up', then 'down', is left holding the question. Audible on any speaker. Not heard by me.

v13 96.24 (seeds 0/11 96.24/96.22 vs v12 95.66/95.65): a cleaner frame for the pairs. Since the time-play and the both-ways Risset pairs went in, Both Ways' 340-880 Hz had piled up 6 dB over the tape and 3 kHz sat 9 dB short. A broad 3 dB dip at 700 Hz and the presence lift moved to 3 kHz at +9 dB (from 3.2 kHz +7) give the Shepard pairs and the seven-cycle rim their edges back: spectrum 94 -> 98, flow to both neighbours up (64 -> 67). Not heard by me.

v14 96.23 (seeds 0/11 96.23/96.21, level with v13 re-scored 96.22/96.20), kept on judgment: THE HARMONY EVOLVES, for Harry's 1 Nov steer ('very simple progressions of 4, 8, 16 bars'). Both Ways turned the same four chords every two bars for the whole track. Now they move in uneven spans of five bars or more and change as the track goes: the first groove 8/5/7/6/5/9 (E-flat minor 9, C-flat major 7 sharp 11, A-flat minor 9, E-flat minor growing its eleventh, a borrowed F half-diminished, B-flat 7 flat 9); the second 6/5/7/6 with the TRITONE SUBSTITUTE - F-flat major 7 sharp 11, B-flat's tritone twin, the harmony itself going both ways in a track about the tritone; the last groove 6/5/5/8/8, its eight bars a tritone away (A minor) now one held chord, then eight bars of B-flat 7 flat 9 leading home. Not heard by me.

v15 95.83 (seeds 0/11 95.83/95.66, level with v14 95.90/95.80): BOTH WAYS, SIDE BY SIDE. The tritone paradox's answer (up or down?) depends on where the Shepard tones' spectral envelope sits; Both Ways crossfades a low-centred envelope to a high-centred one so the stair turns round, and in the last groove sounds both at once. Until now both sat in the centre, one blur. Now, in the last groove, they part: the low-centred pairs drift left and the high-centred right, so the stair that many ears hear going one way sits on one side and the one heard going the other way on the other - legible on speakers as well as headphones. They are widest for the eight bars a tritone away, then close back to the centre over the groove's last eight bars: one question again before the seam. Measured soloed: the low envelope +10 dB left in the tritone bars, the high 4 dB right. Not heard by me.
